executiveSummary: Available reporting indicates a confirmed cyberattack at a U.S. port authority and persistent GNSS interference across multiple sea lanes are the most operationally relevant maritime cyber risks this period. Confidence: medium-high.

vendors: Technologies: Terminal Operating Systems, automated ship-to-shore cranes, port scanning/inspection systems, logistics data platforms, GNSS receivers, AIS-dependent situational awareness.
Named platforms from advisory: LOGINK (logistics platform), Nuctech (scanners), automated STS cranes (various vendors). MARAD Advisory

keyFindings: NC Ports shifted to manual operations after a cyberattack, causing processing delays across multiple facilities.
USCG NAVCEN reported a Baltic Sea GPS interference case with no identified benign cause.
Industry research emphasizes scale and safety risk of GNSS jamming/spoofing for the maritime sector.
MARAD highlights risks from foreign-manufactured logistics platforms, scanners, and automated cranes.

topThreats.action: Disruption at Wilmington, Morehead City, and Charlotte Inland Port demonstrates material impact to U.S. maritime logistics. Operational impact: Manual processing, delays; no evidence of OT compromise. Recommended attention: Validate port partner connectivity, review EDI/API trust, and update incident runbooks for manual gate/yard continuity. Confidence: High Domain: Ports & Terminals Supply Chain Impact: Confirmed

Logistics platforms, scanners, and automated cranes may introduce cyber and national-security exposure to port IT/OT. Operational impact: Potential data compromise, remote access abuse, and operational disruption pathways. Recommended attention: Conduct supplier risk assessments; segment crane/ICS networks; monitor remote vendor sessions. Confidence: High Domain: Port IT/OT Supply Chain Impact: Confirmed

Official anomaly indicates ongoing maritime GNSS risk without benign explanation. Operational impact: Possible loss of position integrity; increased bridge workload and risk to navigation safety margins. Recommended attention: Employ radar/visual fixes, gyro/dead-reckoning, and ECDIS cross-checks; log and report anomalies. Confidence: High Domain: Navigation Safety Impact: Possible

Scale of disruption implies persistent operational risk to global shipping. Operational impact: Route planning and watchkeeping complexity; potential for position spoofing misleads. Recommended attention: Elevate bridge team training and cross-sensor validation procedures. Confidence: Medium Domain: Navigation Navigation Impact: Confirmed

Advisory provides practical crew precautions for jamming/spoofing hotspots. Operational impact: Increased false targets, track jumps, or loss of satellite lock; potential schedule knock-on effects. Recommended attention: Enable ECDIS alarms, monitor AIS consistency, and record anomalies for port state or flag reporting. Confidence: Medium Domain: Navigation & Situational Awareness Safety Impact: Possible

descriptions: NC Ports incident: Disruption of enterprise IT leading to manualized operational workflows; specific intrusion techniques not reported (no confirmed MITRE mappings). Source
GNSS threats: Jamming (denial of satellite signals) and spoofing (deceptive positioning) affecting navigation integrity; formal ATT&CK technique IDs not assigned in sources.
Supply-chain exposure: Potential remote access abuse and data exfiltration via logistics/inspection equipment supply chains; no specific malware reported. MARAD Advisory

outlook72h: GNSS interference: Continued sporadic reports are likely in known hotspots; operators should maintain enhanced navigation cross-checks and anomaly reporting. Confidence: medium. USCG NAVCEN Threat Advisory Port IT disruptions: Additional disclosures or service updates may emerge as investigations mature; immediate risk to OT remains unconfirmed. Confidence: medium. Supporting Report Supply-chain controls: Expect inquiries and potential mitigations around foreign-manufactured port systems following MARAD guidance; immediate operational changes may focus on remote-access oversight. Confidence: high. MARAD Advisory
